title: GNSS jammer geolocation from DF bearings to TAK
summary: Locates a GNSS interference source from KrakenSDR-style direction-of-arrival bearings taken at two fixed sites and one moving vehicle, with noise and multipath outliers. A stdlib robust least-squares triangulation (RANSAC + Gauss-Newton + outlier rejection) runs alongside Stone Soup particle filter and UKF estimators; the fix and its 95% error ellipse go out as Cursor-on-Target events (point + u-d-c-e ellipse) so the emitter can be reported on ATAK/WinTAK. An adapter reads the real krakensdr_doa JSON (websocket) and CSV (DOA_value.html) outputs with the bearing convention taken from its source.
verified: Ran 2026-11-06: 11 unittest cases OK with python3.14.7 stdlib (geo, Kraken JSON/CSV parsing incl. HTTP poll against a local server, triangulation, ellipse, CoT build, UDP send to localhost); locate.py --method all ran with Python 3.12.14 + stonesoup 1.9.1 on synthetic data, outputs in README. Not run: a live KrakenSDR, the websocket listener (needs websockets), and rendering of the CoT ellipse on an ATAK/WinTAK client (ellipse angle convention unverified).
